lines.narration: In this town, nobody claps until morning.
One night a year, Main Street becomes a stage.
And every window fills with faces.
The baker just played the best reel of her life.
Silence. She bowed anyway.
'Not yet,' the mayor said, like I was the strange one.
A kid clapped once, and half the street grabbed his wrists.
They aren't cold people.
They cheer. They whistle. They just never clap.
This year, the fiddler's last note hung in the air like it was waiting.
So I clapped.
Once. The sound came back wrong. Too loud.
Like the street itself clapped with me.
Wait. Every window on the street went dark at the same time.
You see, the hill behind the town listens all year.
Applause isn't praise here. It's payment.
They were never saving their applause for the dancers.
They were saving it for the hill. And now it knows my hands.
This morning, I heard the whole town applaud the sunrise.
It sounded less like joy, and more like rent.
